name: Loratadine
executiveSummary: Second-generation H1 antihistamine with little sedation. Adults and > 12 years or > 30 kg: 10 mg PO/day; children 2–12 years ≤ 30 kg: 5 mg PO/day. Not routine under 2 years.
indications:
## Indications

- Allergic rhinoconjunctivitis (seasonal or perennial).
- Chronic idiopathic urticaria / symptomatic relief of associated pruritus.

## Precautions

- Severe hepatic impairment: start on **alternate days** (same dose per intake).
- Not routinely recommended under 2 years (off-label / not established per label).
- Little sedation at usual doses; caution when combined with other CNS depressants or alcohol.

> Choose syrup or tablet by weight; the 10 mg tablet is not suitable if ≤ 30 kg.

adulto.dose: **10 mg PO once daily**. Severe hepatic impairment: **10 mg on alternate days**.
adulto.administration: PO with or without food, with water.
adulto.notes: Do not exceed the recommended daily dose; no extra benefit and more adverse effects.

pediatrico.presentation: Syrup 1 mg/mL; tablets 10 mg (≥ 30 kg / ≥ 6–12 years per label).
pediatrico.dose: Ages 2–12 and weight **≤ 30 kg**: **5 mg PO once daily** (5 mL of 1 mg/mL syrup). Weight **> 30 kg** or > 12 years: **10 mg PO once daily**. Severe hepatic impairment: same dose on alternate days.
pediatrico.administration: PO. Use the syrup syringe/doser. 10 mg tablet only if weight > 30 kg.
pediatrico.notes: Under 2 years: not recommended unless exceptional product-specific medical indication. Check local label minimum age (some tablet labels state ≥ 6 years).

neonatal.dose: Do not use in neonates or young infants.

stability:
## Stability / storage

- Syrup/tablets: room temperature per label; bottle tightly closed.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Headache, fatigue, dry mouth, nervousness (children); rare sedation at usual doses. Infrequent hypersensitivity reactions.
